title: add-benchmark-lab-memory-profiling-runners-reporting-pipeline
author: Priya Patel
release_notes: Adds memory-profiling workload runners, baseline collectors, and a reporting pipeline for Benchmark Lab. No user-facing API changes. Improves memory regression detection for multi-variant runs.
description: Motivation: We need better memory regression coverage across our representative workload suite. This PR adds memory-profiling runners that exercise peak working set and cold-start memory paths, integrates baseline collectors, and wires results into the existing reporting pipeline used by Benchmark Lab. Summary of changes: (1) new workload runners (benchmark-lab/runners/memory_*) that run representative prompt sets under controlled sequence lengths and batch sizes; (2) a lightweight memory-baseline collector service that samples pmap/cgroup stats and feeds the results to the reporting pipeline; (3) pipeline additions to aggregate, normalize, and visualize memory baselines alongside latency/profiling baselines; (4) docs and runbooks for how to add new memory workloads. Checklist: - [x] Add memory workload runner harness and unit tests - [x] Add baseline collector and e2e integration test against local reporter - [x] Add reporting pipeline steps and dashboards - [x] Add docs + runbook - [x] Performance smoke tests run in CI How to run locally: ./benchmark-lab/bin/run_memory_runner --profile baseline --model gpt-like --batch 4 --seq 2048 Steps to review: focus on runner harness ergonomics, collector overhead, and report schema stability. Related: builds on the adaptive-batching work (ENG-2052) and addresses several items from the production profiling recap (ENG-2187).
commits_summary: 1) Add memory workload runners and harness (benchmark-lab/runners/memory_runner.py) 2) Implement memory-baseline collector service (benchmark-lab/collectors/memory_collector.py) 3) Extend reporting pipeline to accept memory baselines (benchmark-lab/reporting/memory_aggregator.py) 4) Add dashboard JSON and alert rules (observability/dashboards/benchmark_lab_memory.json) 5) Tests and docs
file_snippets: memory_runner.py: add MemoryRunner class that wraps runner harness and exposes --seq/--batch flags
memory_collector.py: sampling loop collects /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.max_usage_in_bytes and process RSS every 250ms
memory_aggregator.py: normalize peak_rss by model_seq_tokens and join with existing latency baselines
review_comments: Ethan Park: Nice addition — can we make the collector sampling interval configurable via env var? Currently 250ms might be too aggressive for large fleets.
Priya Patel (author): Made SAMPLING_INTERVAL env var and defaulted to 250ms. Added documentation in runbook explaining tradeoffs.
Ava Chen: Tests look good. Two suggestions: (1) ensure aggregator tolerates missing baseline for new model variants, (2) add a small e2e CI job to run the collector on a cheap instance policy.
Priya Patel: Added defensive logic and pushed a new workflow that runs an e2e smoke job on the free-tier kube pool. CI passed locally.
Diego Morales: Approved — verified dashboard renders with sample data and alert thresholds look sane. Small nit: rename metric memory_baseline_peak -> benchmark_memory_peak for consistency.
Priya Patel: Renamed metric and updated references. Thanks for the review!
merge_commit_message:
Add memory profiling runners, collector, and reporting pipeline for benchmark lab

- Adds memory_runner, memory_collector, memory_aggregator
- Adds dashboards, alerts, and docs
- Adds CI smoke workflow
notes: This PR expands Benchmark Lab coverage to include memory regressions. The reporting schema adds a new optional field 'memory_peak_bytes' which downstream consumers should handle gracefully. Ops: rollout to staging first and monitor benchmark_lab_memory.alerts for noisy signals.
